description: Mechanical Engineering Students seeking the win
summary:
FlareSense is an advanced geospatial intelligence platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge to safeguard forest and agricultural ecosystems from devastating wildfires, using Jordan's vital green lungs (Ajloun, Jerash, and Dibeen forests) as a high-stakes pilot deployment.

What we developed: An automated data pipeline and interactive web platform powered 100% by NASA FIRMS active fire telemetry from four satellite instruments (Terra/Aqua MODIS and Suomi-NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21 VIIRS). The system features a signature Burning Activity Calendar, a smart visual matrix that reveals the region's thermal pulse and distinguishes routine agricultural residue burning from critical forest fire anomalies.

How it addresses the challenge: By integrating orbital remote sensing with historical baselines, it bridges the gap between raw satellite data and emergency management.

Why it is important: It equips Civil Defense, the Ministry of Agriculture, and emergency planners with precise thermal anomaly detection and predictive analytics, shifting wildfire management from reactive firefighting to proactive, life-saving prevention—with an architecture fully scalable to protect ecosystems globally.
details:
How It Works & Technical Architecture

FlareSense is a proactive geospatial intelligence platform designed to monitor, analyze, and forecast wildfire activity. While utilizing Jordan's critical forest and agricultural belts (Ajloun, Jerash, and Dibeen forests) as a high-stakes pilot deployment, the platform transforms raw orbital satellite telemetry into actionable operational insights. Built 100% on near real-time (NRT) active fire data from NASA FIRMS, our backend pipeline fuses observations from four satellite instruments: Terra/Aqua MODIS and Suomi-NPP, NOAA-20, and NOAA-21 VIIRS. Furthermore, the pipeline is engineered to ingest the complete MODIS historical archive (2000–Present), establishing a 25+ year baseline to model long-term seasonal fire cycles.

Core Innovation: The Burning Activity Calendar

Instead of overwhelming emergency responders with raw coordinate lists, FlareSense introduces the Burning Activity Calendar—a smart visual matrix that reveals the region's "thermal pulse" at a single glance. By cross-referencing live detections with historical baselines, it automatically distinguishes between predictable, routine seasonal agricultural residue burning and critical, out-of-season forest fire anomalies, eliminating false alarms.

Benefits & Intended Impact

FlareSense shifts wildfire management from reactive firefighting to proactive prevention across three key stakeholders:

  • Civil Defense: Provides precise GPS coordinates and early thermal warnings in steep, rugged terrain, drastically reducing dispatch times.
  • Ministry of Agriculture: Clarifies agricultural burning patterns along forest buffers and aids in post-fire ecological damage assessment.
  • Emergency Managers: Enables data-driven forecasting of peak fire seasons to pre-position firefighting crews and equipment before heatwaves strike. Because our architecture runs on global NASA satellite feeds, it is inherently borderless and scalable to protect vulnerable ecosystems worldwide.

Tools, Languages & Development Factors

We developed FlareSense using Python for data ingestion, harmonization, and anomaly modeling, alongside HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript with interactive geospatial mapping libraries for the web interface, supported by AI-assisted coding tools for rapid prototyping. Key factors considered by our team included multi-sensor fusion (combining MODIS broad coverage with VIIRS 375m high spatial resolution to maximize detection confidence), operational practicality to filter out legal agricultural burns, and designing a scalable pipeline capable of expanding beyond our Jordan pilot study to global regions.
